title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 28-30 of Grothendieck's numbering, written around La Longue Marche, 1981). The previous page states a 'Conjecture fondamentale sur les modèles'. Let U be an elementary anabelian variety, i.e. a successive fibration in hyperbolic curves, over a number field. Let V be regular of finite type over Q. Let f: E_V = π_1(V) → E_U = π_1(U) be an outer homomorphism compatible with the projections to Γ_Q. The conjecture says two conditions are equivalent: (a) f comes, up to isomorphism, from a unique morphism V → U; (b) f restricted to E_V^0 is 'anabelian', meaning the image of every open subgroup has trivial centralizer.

This page proceeds in four steps.
(1) Necessity of (b), i.e. (a) ⇒ (b). Any open subgroup of E_V contains an open subgroup of the decomposition group of some closed point v of V. The centralizer of a larger subgroup is contained in the centralizer of a smaller one. So it suffices to treat V = Spec k(v), a point, where the question becomes the 'question préliminaire' of earlier pages.
(2) This yields an explicitly labelled 'conséquence conjecturale'. Let Γ' ⊂ Im(E_U → Γ_Q) be open, corresponding to a number field k. A k-point of U gives a section s: Γ' → E_U, hence an action of Γ' on π_U = π_1(U_{\bar Q}). Then π_U^{Γ'} = {1}: the centralizer in the geometric fundamental group of the image of a rational-point section is trivial.
(3) A programmatic sentence: the relation between this consequence and the earlier conjecture on the groups E_K (the birational / function-field version) is to be studied later.
(4) The model conjecture implies the 'conjecture fondamentale sur les corps', provided the field version is restricted to homomorphisms compatible with the filtrations modelled on U. These are presumably the decomposition/inertia filtrations at the boundary of the model. More generally one may take schemes that are projective limits of elementary anabelian models with affine transition morphisms. The next page continues this, e.g. V = spectra of local rings of points of U, so that dominant morphisms correspond to suitable outer homomorphisms.

In modern terms, the page links the Hom-form of the anabelian conjecture with the section conjecture and the birational anabelian conjecture. The 'trivial centralizer of images of open subgroups' is proposed as the intrinsic group-theoretic criterion singling out geometric homomorphisms, including non-dominant ones. For V a point, (a)⇔(b) is a form of the section conjecture.
errors: No mathematical error. The reduction of (a)⇒(b) to the point case is sound: an open subgroup of E_V contains an open part of a decomposition group, and centralizers shrink as subgroups grow.

The consequence π_U^{Γ'} = 1 actually holds for any section, not only those from rational points. For hyperbolic curves the Galois module H_1 (and the graded pieces of central series) has negative weights, so no section can have invariants. Hence for V a point, condition (b) holds automatically for all sections, and (a)⇔(b) reduces exactly to the section conjecture. The page does not remark this, nor whether (b) is a genuine restriction only in positive-dimensional V.
It is ambiguous whether the centralizer in (b) is taken in E_U or in π_U. Taking it in E_U also needs slimness of the relevant Galois groups, which is true but unstated.

ideas.what: Reduction of the necessity of the centralizer condition to the case of a point (rational-point sections)
ideas.modern_name: decomposition groups / sections of π_1 attached to rational points

ideas.what: Triviality of Γ'-invariants of the geometric π_1 under the action defined by a rational-point section, for elementary anabelian U
ideas.modern_name: trivial centralizer of section images / Galois-centralizer-freeness (weight argument)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (1990s, Galois rigidity), Tamagawa, Mochizuki; Hoshi–Mochizuki for configuration spaces and iterated fibrations

ideas.what: Characterizing geometric homomorphisms (including non-dominant ones) by the condition that images of open subgroups have trivial centralizers
ideas.modern_name: Hom-form anabelian conjecture combined with section conjecture; 'nondegenerate' homomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, open homs ↔ dominant maps); Mochizuki 1999 proved the dominant/open Hom version for hyperbolic curve targets over sub-p-adic fields
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states Hom-conjecture and section conjecture; the centralizer criterion in this form is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Model (Hom) conjecture implies birational/field conjecture when restricted to filtration-compatible homomorphisms; passage to pro-schemes (limits of models with affine transitions, local rings)
ideas.modern_name: birational anabelian geometry via pro-varieties; decomposition/inertia-compatible homomorphisms (cf. Pop's birational anabelian theorem)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche discusses birational anabelian conjecture; this exact implication unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes the centralizer-triviality of images of open subgroups as a criterion for an outer Galois-compatible homomorphism E_V → E_U to be geometric, for arbitrary regular V and not just dominant maps. The literature mainly treats 'open homomorphisms ↔ dominant morphisms' (Mochizuki) and sections separately. Whether a centralizer-type condition characterizes geometric homomorphisms for non-dominant maps from positive-dimensional V (e.g. maps contracting V onto a curve inside U, or constant maps) seems not to have been systematically formulated or studied.
missed.quote: b) f | E_V^0 est anabélien, i.e. l'image par f de tout sous-groupe ouvert de E_V^0 a un centralisateur réduit à 1 ... Pour la nécessité de b), on est ramené aussitôt au cas où V est réduite à un pt
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a uniform group-theoretic formulation bridging the Hom-conjecture and the section conjecture for all morphisms. Testing whether (b) is really the right condition (e.g. for homomorphisms factoring through a curve of U) could be a well-posed question in current anabelian geometry.

missed.claim: Explicit statement that the model-version Hom conjecture implies the field (birational) version once one restricts to homomorphisms compatible with filtrations modelled on U, via pro-schemes that are limits of elementary anabelian models.
missed.quote: La conjecture fondamentale sur les modèles implique la conjecture fondamentale sur les corps, à condition ... de se limiter aux [hom.] compatibles aux filtrations, modelés par U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is broadly anticipated by later work (Pop, Mochizuki on pro-curves/local rings), so likely of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds an unpublished formulation of a combined Hom/section anabelian conjecture with a centralizer criterion, plus the conjectural (now known, via weights) triviality of section centralizers. The individual ingredients are known to specialists. The centralizer criterion for non-dominant maps from higher-dimensional V is a mildly notable detail not standard in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'se limiter aux lieux compatibles aux filtrations' — 'lieux' is more likely 'hom.' (homomorphismes), i.e. 'se limiter aux hom. compatibles aux filtrations, modelées par U'.
'prenant des schémas qui sont des lieux de modèles élém. anabéliens' — 'lieux' is very likely 'limites' (consistent with the next page: 'schéma-limite ... morphismes de transition affines').
'ou compléments de des transitions' — likely 'avec morphismes de transition affines' or similar.
Marginal note likely begins 'et il est naturel de se borner à l'équivalence de a) et b) — la condition c) ...' rather than 'inspection'.
